title: LVM lab: physical volumes, groups, logical volumes and snapshots
summary: One server with three empty 2 GiB disks beside its system disk, there to be used up and wiped. The exercises turn the disks into physical volumes, pool them in a volume group, carve logical volumes with ext4 and xfs, grow a mounted one online, take a snapshot and roll a change back, then tear everything down. Never type the disk names: every block starts from DISKS, the 2G whole disks lsblk lists (today vda, vdb and vdc; the system disk is vdd, the last on the virtio bus). Ported from qlab's lvm-lab.

exercises.title: LVM anatomy
exercises.text: Three layers: physical volumes (disks or partitions labelled for LVM), a volume group that pools them, logical volumes cut from the pool. The system disk is not LVM here; the three lab disks are empty.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the three lab disks, never the system one
lsblk    # the 10G disk with partitions is the system (vdd); the three 2G ones are the lab's
sudo pvs; sudo vgs; sudo lvs    # nothing yet
sudo wipefs -n $DISKS    # no signature: empty disks

exercises.title: Physical volumes and a volume group
exercises.text: pvcreate writes the LVM label on each disk; vgcreate pools them. The group's size is the sum, minus a little metadata.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the three lab disks, never the system one
sudo vgs labvg    # about 6 GiB, 3 PVs

exercises.title: Logical volumes with ext4 and xfs
exercises.text: A logical volume is a block device like a partition, but it can span disks and change size.

commands: sudo lvcreate -L 1G -n data labvg && sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/labvg/data
sudo lvcreate -L 1G -n logs labvg && sudo mkfs.xfs /dev/labvg/logs

exercises.title: Grow a volume while it is mounted
exercises.text: lvextend --resizefs grows the logical volume and the file system on it in one step, online. ext4 and xfs both grow online; only ext4 can also shrink (offline).

commands: df -h /mnt/lab-data && cat /mnt/lab-data/keep    # 2 GiB, the data still there

exercises.title: Snapshot and rollback
exercises.text: A snapshot records the origin as it was; merging it back undoes every change made since. The merge completes when the origin is not in use.

commands: echo version-2 | sudo tee /mnt/lab-data/file    # the change to undo
sudo lvchange -an labvg/data && sudo lvchange -ay labvg/data && sudo mount /dev/labvg/data /mnt/lab-data

exercises.title: Tear it all down
exercises.text: Back to three empty disks: unmount, remove the group (and its volumes), remove the PV labels, wipe what is left.

commands: DISKS=$(lsblk -dnpo NAME,SIZE,TYPE | awk '$2=="2G" && $3=="disk" {print $1}' | xargs); echo $DISKS    # the three lab disks, never the system one
